The trip in one look

The ship is the destination. Flights and hotel are logistics; Star, CocoCay, ports, restaurants and shows are what make the money feel defensible.

Travel flow

Fly Bermuda to Orlando on July 17, stay one night at The Alfond Inn, then transfer to Port Canaveral for Star of the Seas on July 18.

Room setup

Matt & Steph plus child, Kris & Tariq plus 2 kids, and Peter & Judy. All three rooms are Ocean View Balcony quotes from Royal Caribbean.

Trip shape

One private-island day, three Western Caribbean port days, two sea days for the ship itself, then return to Orlando on July 25.

Day-by-day itinerary

Balanced enough for kids, adults and the people who just want not to be dragged through a military-grade vacation schedule.

Jul 17BDA -> Orlando. Alfond Inn overnight.
Jul 18Transfer to Port Canaveral. Board Star of the Seas.
Jul 19Perfect Day at CocoCay, Bahamas.
Jul 20At sea. Waterpark, pools, shows, restaurants.
Jul 21Cozumel, Mexico.
Jul 22Roatan, Honduras.
Jul 23Costa Maya, Mexico.
Jul 24At sea. Last full ship day.
Jul 25Arrive Port Canaveral. Fly MCO -> BDA or stay one more night.

Ports worth caring about

Do one big excursion, one beach or snorkel day, one low-pressure wander, and make CocoCay the premium cabana day.

CocoCay

Royal's private island. This is the day to spend up for comfort.

  • Coco Beach Club cabana or overwater cabana
  • Beach Club infinity pool and upgraded lunch
  • Thrill Waterpark for kids/teens
  • Oasis Lagoon, Splashaway Bay, Chill Island

Cozumel

Best for easy beach clubs or water days.

  • Nachi Cocom / Mr. Sanchos style beach club
  • Snorkel or catamaran
  • Jeep/island tour
  • Ruins if people want a longer day

Roatan

The nature/adventure stop.

  • West Bay beach
  • Reef snorkeling
  • Sloths, monkeys and island tour
  • Zipline or private driver day

Costa Maya

Lowest-stress port for mixed ages.

  • Port pool and shopping
  • Maya Chan / beach club day
  • Chacchoben ruins
  • Keep it flexible if people are tired

Perfect Day premium plan

If the budget allows, make this the cabana day. For a family-heavy trip, Coco Beach Club is the cleaner premium choice than Hideaway Beach because Hideaway is adult-focused and this trip includes kids.

Coco Beach Club cabanas usually include Beach Club admission for cabana guests, dedicated attendant service, upgraded lunch, infinity pool access and a quieter beach setup.

Cabana call

Best target: Coco Beach Club cabana. Dream target: overwater cabana if pricing is not completely deranged.

Reason: adults get a nicer base, kids still get island fun, and CocoCay becomes the premium anchor of the whole trip.

The ship areas

Star works because everyone can split naturally: kids to water and clubs, adults to pools and restaurants, everyone back together for shows and port days.

Thrill IslandCategory 6 slides, Crown's Edge, FlowRider, rock wall and mini golf.
Chill IslandPools, loungers, Lime & Coconut and an easy sea-day base.
SurfsideFamily zone with splash areas, carousel, kid food and parent-friendly bars.
AquaDomeOcean views, AquaTheater shows, Hooked and AquaDome Market.
Central ParkQuieter green space, specialty dining, bars and night strolls.
Royal PromenadePearl, shopping, pizza, bars, music and people-watching.

Kids, waterpark and family stuff

This is the strongest reason to pick Star over a regular cruise ship. Sea days are not filler. They are the point.

Category 6 waterpark

Six-slide waterpark on Thrill Island. This is the headline kid and teen energy burner.

Surfside

Family neighborhood with splash play, carousel, casual food and places where adults can sit without pretending standing around is relaxing.

Adventure Ocean and teens

Royal's kids club programming plus teen hangout spaces. Useful for grown-up dinners or just decompression.

Shows and nights out

Flagship entertainment is a real part of the value. This is not just buffet, pool, bed, repeat.

AquaDome

Torque and Pirates & Mermaids style water, diving, acrobatics and tech-heavy spectacle.

Absolute Zero

SOL ice show in the ship's ice arena.

Royal Theater

Back to the Future: The Musical plus Royal's original productions. Reserve headline shows early in the app.

Food and premium dining

Included food covers plenty. The specialty dining package is for better adult dinners, variety, and a few family meals that feel like an event. The photos below are actual Royal Caribbean dining shots, not generic filler.

Included staples

Main Dining Room, Windjammer and Surfside

Use these for volume: easy breakfasts, kid-friendly lunches, casual dinners and no-extra-cost backups when the group splits up. Surfside is the family win because it keeps food close to the kids' area.

Fast casual

AquaDome Market, Pearl Cafe, Park Cafe and Sorrento's

Good for snack runs, coffee, pizza, lighter bites and avoiding a full sit-down meal. This is where the ship feels easier with kids because nobody has to coordinate a whole production.

Specialty dinners

Chops Grille, Hooked Seafood and Giovanni's

Best use of the dining package for the adults. Chops is the steakhouse anchor, Hooked is the seafood night, and Giovanni's is the safe group-friendly Italian pick.

Event meals

Izumi Hibachi, Celebration Table and Empire Supper Club

Izumi is the obvious fun family specialty meal. Celebration Table is better for a private-feeling group dinner. Empire Supper Club is the splurge adult night if people want one serious dinner.

Included staples

Main Dining, Windjammer, Surfside Eatery, AquaDome Market, Pearl Cafe, Park Cafe, El Loco Fresh and Sorrento's.

Premium picks

Chops, Hooked, Izumi, Giovanni's, Lincoln Park Supper Club, Celebration Table, Pier 7, Desserted and Playmakers-style spots.

Smart use

Book 2-3 adult dinners, one easy family specialty meal, then keep breakfast and lunch casual.

Cost breakdown

Each family/couple pays their own room, flights, hotel share and packages. Package pricing is now calculated from the quoted per-person rates.

Deluxe drink package

$78/adult/day

Assumes both adults in each room buy it for all 7 cruise nights. Kids are not included in this package calculation.

Dining package

$357/adult + $76/child

Total package price, not daily. This is the specialty dining add-on for planned Chops, Hooked, Izumi and family dining moments.

The Key

$50/guest/day

Assumes every guest buys it for all 7 cruise nights. Useful for priority boarding perks, internet and smoother logistics.

Verdict

Expensive, yes. But coherent. The ship is the destination, and that makes the price much easier to defend.

Why it works

Star is built for families without punishing adults: waterpark, kids club, private island, proper shows, tons of food and enough spaces to split up.

Main risk

The drink, dining and Key packages are now priced in. Remaining creep is excursions, Wi-Fi, arcade, photos, cabana upgrades and the return hotel.

My call

Worth presenting as the frontrunner. Just keep add-ons intentional or the total gets spicy fast.
